messages:
Anna: quick sync — proposing we standardize on doing trace_id enrichment at the collector ingress (otel collector) rather than relying on app libs to always emit it. reasoning below, want quick takes :thinking:
Mike: curious — what's the main driver? i thought app-level structured logging was the long-term goal so apps own the field.
Anna: long-term yes; short-term ops + compatibility: we have a ton of services (legacy gorilla/mux + some node lambdas) that don't emit structured JSON or the 32-hex trace_id. if the collector can parse `traceparent` / `b3` headers and attach a `trace_id` field to the log envelope before export, we get instant joinability in Console without changing every repo.
Dina: collector enrichment sounds low-friction. couple caveats: 1) log parsing rules differ (text vs json) so we must avoid duplicating trace ids or mis-parsing. 2) sampling: if span was sampled-out, do we still attach trace_id?
Anna: agreed. proposal: always attach trace_id when header present (even if sampled-out) — we need correlation for debugging cold path issues. we won't create spans in collector, only add field to logs/metrics envelopes.
Samir: we also need header normalization. some clients send `x-request-id` (uuid), some `traceparent`, some `x-b3-traceid`. we should canonicalize to the Otel 32-char hex lowercase `trace_id`. code snippet for collector processor idea:
```
processors:
  enrich_traceid:
    match: 
      - attributes: {http.request.headers: ".*"}
    extract_traceparent: true
    normalize_to: trace_id  # 32 hex chars
```
Mike: normalization is good. watch out for 16-char b3 ids (64-bit) — convert by left-padding with zeros to 32 hex chars so joins work.
Lucy: important: privacy/PII checks. if we attach trace_id at ingestion, ensure the pipeline doesn't try to store whole headers as searchable text. store only the canonical `trace_id` string. also add ACLs so private logs aren't accidentally exported to hosted telemetry.
observability-bot: pipeline-config-change requested by @Anna - ticket RED-TELE-412 created: "collector: add trace_id enrichment + normalization" (link: https://redwood.atlassian.com/browse/RED-TELE-412)
Dina: related ingestion concern: cardinality. trace_id as a field is high-cardinality by definition but it's essential for joins. make sure our indexing model treats it as a keyword (no aggregation cardinality explosion). also retention notes: storing trace_id doesn't increase volume much but enabling per-trace index lookups may require new index patterns.
Samir: on dashboards: Console should have a "trace timeline" pane that can show logs + spans by trace_id. for rollout, we should add a toggle on per-route dashboards to join by `trace_id` and fall back to request-id.
Anna: rollout checklist (draft):
- [ ] Collector processor deployed to staging parsing `traceparent`/`b3`/`x-request-id`
- [ ] Normalization implemented: 32-hex canonical trace_id (left-pad b3 16-char ids)
- [ ] Apps: gradual opt-in to emit `trace_id` in structured logs (python/node libs)
- [ ] Console: add join-by-trace_id UI and trace timeline widget (canary dashboards)
- [ ] Index changes: trace_id as keyword field, shard template update
- [ ] Backfill plan for recent logs if needed (only metadata, not full content)
Mike: question about older logs: backfilling trace_id won't be possible for unstructured logs unless we reprocess raw payloads and reconstruct headers — big job. maybe we only backfill for services using our sidecar.
Lucy: also audit: make sure downstream exporters (s3, splunk) don't suddenly receive a new field that breaks parsers. add exporter schema bump and compatibility flag.
Samir: alerting changes: many of our existing alerts use `request_id` dimensions. we'll add companion alerts with `trace_id` where appropriate and keep old ones for a month then remove.
Dina: technical nit: ensure we use RFC `traceparent` parsing (W3C trace-context). some libs send uppercase hex; normalize to lowercase. also avoid adding `trace_id` for logs that already have `trace_id` — dedupe logic.
Anna: final note on sampling: even if the trace is not sampled, having the trace_id allows us to link across logs and then request the full trace from retainers if available. so we keep it.
Mike: +1. we should document the header precedence: traceparent > b3 > x-request-id. publish a runbook snippet e.g.:
```
if traceparent present: parse and extract trace_id (32 hex)
else if b3 present: extract, pad to 32 hex
else if x-request-id looks like hex32: use as trace_id
else: no trace_id added
```
Anna: thanks all. I'll update RED-TELE-412 with the checklist and schedule a 30-min sync to pick owners for each bullet. tagging @Samir for dashboard work and @Lucy for exporter compatibility tests. :thumbsup:
